title: Creating PROTACs and RIPTACs: Tim Shannon on The Long Run - TimmermanReport.com
gist: This is a podcast intro page for The Long Run Ep212 with Canaan Partners general partner Tim Shannon. With Yale's Craig Crews, Shannon built Arvinas, which develops PROTAC targeted protein degraders, and then Halda Therapeutics, whose 'hold and kill' RIPTAC degraders led Johnson & Johnson to acquire it for $3 billion on early prostate cancer results. The episode's theme is that timing a new biotech technology wave matters.

themes.theme: Targeted protein degraders: PROTACs to RIPTACs

insights.claim: Tim Shannon of Canaan Partners and Yale chemist Craig Crews built Arvinas, a New Haven-based developer of PROTACs, a new class of small molecule drugs that work as targeted protein degraders.
insights.so_what: Shows Canaan's track record of founding companies in protein degradation.
insights.locator: Tim got started as a VC
insights.speaker: @ldtimmerman

insights.claim: Johnson & Johnson acquired Halda Therapeutics, co-founded by Tim Shannon and Craig Crews, for $3 billion a little over a year ago, based on encouraging early results in advanced prostate cancer with its RIPTAC 'hold and kill' induced-proximity degraders.
insights.so_what: Big pharma will pay billions for early-stage induced-proximity modalities, which supports valuations in this space.
insights.speaker: @ldtimmerman

insights.claim: Following Halda's $3 billion sale to Johnson & Johnson, many other scientists are trying to build on the success of RIPTAC-style induced-proximity drugs.
insights.so_what: Expect more startups and funding rounds in induced-proximity degraders, which also means more competition.
insights.quote: Many other scientists are seeking to build on this success.
insights.speaker: @ldtimmerman

insights.claim: Luke Timmerman argues that timing matters in biotech: investors and founders should be neither too early nor too late to a new technology wave.
insights.so_what: Entry timing on a modality cycle drives venture returns.
insights.quote: You don’t want to be too early, or too late, when a new technology wave emerges.

insights.claim: Tim Shannon began as a biotech venture capitalist during the Great Financial Crisis, which turned out to be the start of a biotech venture capital boom.
insights.so_what: Investing during downturns can catch the start of a biotech boom.

insights.claim: AlphaSense's healthcare team describes 2026 as a year of transition for life sciences, with battles over oral GLP-1 and targeted radioligand therapy markets and a resurgent biotech IPO market.
insights.so_what: A reopening biotech IPO window improves exit options for venture-backed biotechs; note this comes from sponsor copy.
